request.what: Annual maintenance and enhancement funding for MLabs Core Tool Maintenance & Enhancement: Plutarch and Ply.

claims.claim: The proposal requests 1,162,746 ada, consisting of 1,128,880 ada for Plutarch and Ply maintenance, compatibility, and developer experience plus a 33,866 ada Intersect Budget Administration fee.
Plutarch is described as a Haskell eDSL for creating efficient Cardano smart contracts through controlled compilation into UPLC.
Ply is described as helping serialize Plutarch scripts to and from CIP-57 blueprint-style artifacts with inferred types to protect the on-chain/off-chain boundary.
MLabs states that a recent internal audit found at least 26 teams building with Plutarch and Ply, while the rationale separately states a conservative count of at least 15 teams.
MLabs claims Plutarch scripts rank among the smallest in its public cross-language benchmark suite while requiring comparatively low on-chain compute and memory, and provides a benchmark URL.

The proposed work prioritizes critical breakages and serious vulnerabilities first, then protocol-era and hard-fork compatibility, then bug fixes and optimizations, then documentation and developer-experience improvements.
The document states the proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The document states the requested amount does not, at submission time alone or in aggregate, breach the 350M ada Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713.
The proposal says independent oversight will be provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties, with reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.
The document discloses prior MLabs funding for Plutarch/Ply through Project Catalyst Fund9 and Fund13, plus a prior 70,000 ada Intersect payment to update Plutarch for Conway-era features.

summary: The anchor describes a 1,162,746 ada treasury withdrawal submitted by Intersect for MLabs to maintain and enhance Plutarch and Ply, with some governance, prior-funding, oversight, and external reference claims, but limited budget detail and no complete feasibility, risk, alternatives, or failure-mode analysis.
